drug_indication: BCG-unresponsive Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer with CIS, with or without papillary disease
catalyst_text: Published positive long-term results from Phase 2/3 study
detailed_catalyst_text: A peer-reviewed Journal of Urology publication reported long-term outcomes from the Phase 2/3 QUILT-3.032 trial of ANKTIVA plus BCG in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS, with or without papillary disease. The data showed durable efficacy, including a 71% complete response rate and median CR duration of 26.6 months, along with a favorable safety profile. These results support durable disease control and bladder preservation potential in this high-risk population.
catalyst_text_evidence: ImmunityBio, Inc. ... today announced the publication of long-term data from the Phase 2/3 QUILT-3.032 study (N=100) in the Journal of Urology. The study evaluated ANKTIVA (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) in patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary disease. The treatment continued to demonstrate a favorable safety profile. Most treatment-related adverse events were Grade 1 or Grade 2 and consisted of localized bladder symptoms associated with intravesical therapy. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4% of patients, with no Grade 4 or Grade 5 treatment-related adverse events reported.

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for label expansion in NMIBC
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA expanded the label of ANKTIVA in combination with BCG to include adult patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, including papillary-only tumors. This expansion makes it the first approval covering papillary-only disease in this setting and broadens access to all BCG-unresponsive NMIBC patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: ImmunityBio, Inc. (NASDAQ:IBRX), a commercial-stage immunotherapy company, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has expanded the approved indication for ANKTIVA (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) to include patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with papillary-only tumors. The expanded FDA label reads as follows: ANKTIVA, in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG), is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. This is the first FDA approval to include BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with papillary-only tumors.

catalyst_text: Received UAE approval covering CIS and papillary disease
detailed_catalyst_text: Regulators in the United Arab Emirates granted Marketing Authorization for the 0.4 mg intravesical presentation with BCG to treat BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, spanning CIS with or without papillary tumors and papillary-only disease. This is the first authorization worldwide to include the full spectrum of BCG-unresponsive NMIBC, expanding access and offering an alternative to radical cystectomy in this setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: The Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) granted Marketing Authorization for two ANKTIVA presentations, the broadest approval to date for ANKTIVA including papillary disease and CIS in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer and non-small cell lung cancer in patients who failed checkpoint inhibitors and chemotherapy. Each approval covers a distinct indication: ANKTIVA 0.4 mg/0.4 mL (solution for intravesical instillation) in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC. Per the approved UAE Summary of Product Characteristics, ANKTIVA is indicated with BCG for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors and BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with papillary tumors. Emirates Drug Establishment, Product Marketing Authorization Approval certificates and approved Summaries of Product Characteristics, Registration Nos. 78609-45860-260486 (NMIBC) and 78609-1572-260487 (NSCLC), first registration 2026-07-24.

catalyst_text: Received UAE approval for metastatic lung cancer patients
detailed_catalyst_text: The United Arab Emirates granted Marketing Authorization for the 1.2 mg subcutaneous presentation in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors for adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer after progression on standard therapies. This approval addresses checkpoint-refractory disease with limited options and broadens availability of an immunotherapy approach in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: The Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) granted Marketing Authorization for two ANKTIVA presentations, the broadest approval to date for ANKTIVA including papillary disease and CIS in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer and non-small cell lung cancer in patients who failed checkpoint inhibitors and chemotherapy. Each approval covers a distinct indication: ANKTIVA 1.2 mg/0.6 mL (solution for subcutaneous injection) in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Emirates Drug Establishment, Product Marketing Authorization Approval certificates and approved Summaries of Product Characteristics, Registration Nos. 78609-45860-260486 (NMIBC) and 78609-1572-260487 (NSCLC), first registration 2026-07-24.

catalyst_text: Presented positive outcomes research results at ISPOR 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary health economic analysis results comparing ANKTIVA plus BCG versus TAR-200 in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS were presented at ISPOR 2026. The analysis showed lower costs per sustained complete responder and per cystectomy avoided over up to three years in a U.S. Medicare population, supporting payer value and potential reimbursement.
catalyst_text_evidence: ImmunityBio, Inc. ((IBRX), a commercial-stage immunotherapy company, today announced preliminary results from a new health economic analysis demonstrating that ANKTIVA® (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln; NAI) plus Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) achieved a lower cost per sustained complete responder compared to TAR-200 in patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer carcinoma in situ ± papillary disease (NMIBC CIS). The findings were presented at the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (ISPOR) 2026, 2026-05-17 to 2026-05-20, at the Pennsylvania Convention Center in Philadelphia, by Ruchika Talwar, M.D., Medical Director and Assistant Professor Urologic Oncology at Vanderbilt Health. Cost per cystectomy avoided: ANKTIVA plus BCG demonstrated savings of $109,622 at Year 1, $151,438 at Year 2, and $60,393 at Year 3 compared to TAR-200. Cost per complete responder: Savings of $313,775 at Year 1 and $282,013 at Year 2.

catalyst_text: Presented positive comparative data at AUA meeting
detailed_catalyst_text: Two indirect treatment comparison analyses were presented at AUA 2026 evaluating the therapy plus BCG versus nadofaragene firadenovec and versus TAR-200 in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ. The analyses showed higher anytime and 12-month complete response rates, more than double median duration of response, reduced cystectomy risk versus nadofaragene, and fewer treatment-related adverse events versus TAR-200.
catalyst_text_evidence: ImmunityBio, Inc. ((IBRX), a vertically integrated commercial-stage immunotherapy company, today announced results from two indirect treatment comparison (ITC) analyses presented at the 2026 American Urological Association (AUA) Annual Meeting evaluating nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln (NAI, ANKTIVA®) plus Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) against two other U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved therapies for patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary disease. Podium presentation - PD25-15 (Edwards et al.): NAI+BCG versus nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS with or without papillary disease. Interactive poster - IP50-12 (Jayram et al.): NAI+BCG versus TAR-200 in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS with or without papillary disease. After matching, NAI+BCG demonstrated: Anytime CR rate of 69.7% (weighted) versus 53.4% for nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg; OR 2.01 (95% CI: 1.08, 3.72). Median duration of complete response of 22.1 months versus 9.7 months, a difference of 12.45 months (95% CI: 8.17, 17.09); HR for end of response 0.57 (95% CI: 0.34, 0.95). Cystectomy-free survival HR 0.40 (95% CI: 0.21, 0.75). A separate MAIC was conducted comparing individual patient data from QUILT-3.032 (Cohort A, NAI+BCG, n=100) with aggregate data from SunRISe-1 (Cohort 2, TAR-200, n=85). At 12 months, NAI+BCG achieved a higher complete response rate than TAR-200 (49.2% versus 45.9%; OR 1.14; 95% CI: 0.61, 2.15); the difference did not reach statistical significance. Patients treated with NAI+BCG experienced substantially fewer treatment-related adverse events of any grade than patients treated with TAR-200 (61.7% versus 83.5%), a statistically significant 68% reduction in adverse event odds (OR 0.32; 95% CI: 0.15, 0.67).

The study evaluates adding the agent to BCG in BCG-naïve non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ with or without papillary disease to improve complete response rate. Based on the IDMC review of the interim data, the committee recommended that no additional enrollment beyond N=366 is required and that the study is adequately powered to detect the pre-specified clinically meaningful difference in CR rate at the protocol-specified power. The Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) confirmed that the fully enrolled study (N=366) is adequately powered to detect the pre-specified difference in complete response rate between the experimental and control arms, and that no additional enrollment is required

catalyst_text: Completed enrollment and positive interim analysis results

An FDA-requested interim analysis showed a statistically significant improvement in duration of complete response for the combination with no significant safety concerns. These results strengthen the clinical evidence for the regimen in earlier-stage disease.
catalyst_text_evidence: ImmunityBio (IBRX), a commercial-stage immunotherapy company, today announced completion of enrollment in its Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating ANKTIVA (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) plus Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) versus BCG alone in patients with BCG-naïve non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary tumors. The QUILT 2.005 trial (NCT02138734), which completed enrollment ahead of schedule, includes 366 patients randomized to receive either BCG alone, the current standard-of-care for NMIBC CIS, or ANKTIVA in combination with BCG. An interim analysis requested by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) demonstrated that treatment with ANKTIVA plus BCG resulted in a statistically significant improvement in the duration of complete response compared with BCG alone, with no significant safety concerns reported.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 2 results in recurrent glioblastoma
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 2 results from QUILT-3.078 in second-line recurrent or progressive glioblastoma showed median overall survival not yet reached among 14 evaluable patients, with 19 of 23 patients alive. The regimen increased absolute lymphocyte counts within one cycle and maintained immune competence, and demonstrated a manageable safety profile across 219 doses with three treatment-related serious adverse events. These findings indicate encouraging activity and immune restoration in a high-need population.
catalyst_text_evidence: ImmunityBio, Inc. ((IBRX), a commercial-stage immunotherapy company developing cytokine and cellular immunotherapies designed to restore immune competence, today announced updated Phase 2 clinical results from QUILT 3.078 (NCT06061809), evaluating a chemotherapy-free combination immunotherapy regimen in patients with second-line recurrent or progressive glioblastoma (GBM), as well as patients treated under single-patient INDs (spINDs) across first- to third-line disease. As of 2026-01-22, the study has enrolled 23 patients with recurrent or progressive GBM who progressed following standard-of-care therapy, including surgery, radiation, and temozolomide-based chemotherapy. 19 of the 23 enrolled patients remain alive, with four deaths reported to date. Of the 23 enrolled patients, 14 currently have evaluable clinical data and comprise the efficacy population for the current analysis. The median follow up is 6 months in the evaluable cohort. All four deaths to date occurred within the evaluable cohort, and median overall survival has not yet been reached. ALC increased within one treatment cycle, with mean ALC rising to ≥ 1.4 x 10^3/uL (p <0.001, N=14). ANKTIVA + CAR-NK demonstrated a manageable safety profile following a total of 219 doses administered to date, with three treatment-related serious adverse events reported among 41 GBM patients (2L and 3L+) enrolled across QUILT-3.078 (N=23) and single-patient INDs (N=18).

detailed_catalyst_text: A supplemental BLA for the papillary-only BCG-unresponsive NMIBC indication was initially submitted in 2025. The release also cites peer-reviewed long-term Phase 2/3 results in 80 patients showing a 12-month DFS of 58.2%, a 36-month disease-specific survival of 96%, and over 80% bladder preservation at three years. These findings underscore durable disease control and bladder-sparing potential in this high-risk population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Based on these discussions, the FDA recommended that the Company provide certain additional information for its consideration to support a potential resubmission of the sBLA initially submitted in 2025 for the papillary indication. Long-term data published in The Journal of Urology evaluating ANKTIVA in patients with papillary disease (N=80) demonstrate approximately 96% bladder cancer-specific survival and greater than 80% bladder preservation at three years, with median outcomes not yet reached. As recently published in The Journal of Urology (Chang et al., 2025), the study met its primary endpoint with a 12-month disease-free survival (DFS) rate of 58.2% (95% confidence interval: 46.6-68.2%). Patients treated with intravesical ANKTIVA plus BCG demonstrated a 96.0% disease-specific survival (DSS) rate at 36 months, with the median DSS not yet reached. Notably, the therapy conferred a bladder-sparing benefit: cystectomy-free survival was 92.2% at 12 months and 81.8% at 36 months.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 2b and Phase 3 results
detailed_catalyst_text: The company reported positive clinical results for non-small cell lung cancer from two trials. A randomized Phase 3 study showed a statistically significant and sustained increase in absolute lymphocyte count with the combination versus checkpoint inhibitor alone, and a Phase 2b study showed 77% ALC restoration with improved overall survival in responders. These findings support immune restoration with the regimen and its association with better survival in checkpoint-experienced patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: ImmunityBio, Inc. ((IBRX), a clinical-stage immunotherapy company, today announced positive results from its ANKTIVA (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept) clinical program in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) based on two studies, QUILT-2.023 and QUILT-3.055. In first-line NSCLC (QUILT-2.023), a randomized study demonstrated a statistically significant and sustained increase in absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) from baseline with ANKTIVA plus CPI compared with CPI alone (p=0.0065), establishing ANKTIVA's contribution as a lymphocyte-stimulating agent. In second- and later-line NSCLC (QUILT-3.055), a single-arm study demonstrated restoration or maintenance of ALC ≥1.0 × 10³ cells/µL in 77% of patients receiving ANKTIVA plus CPI (responders). Responders receiving ANKTIVA plus CPI experienced significantly longer overall survival compared with non-responders (median OS 16.2 vs 11.8 months; HR 0.52; p=0.0369), directly linking immune restoration to clinical benefit. Patients achieving higher immune competence (ALC ≥1.2 ×10³ cells/µL) demonstrated additional survival benefit, with median OS of 21.1 months (HR 0.33; p=0.0009), independent of PD-L1 status, exceeding historical overall survival of 7-9 months with standard of care chemotherapy.

drug_indication: BCG-unresponsive papillary-only non-muscle invasive bladder cancer
catalyst_text: Published positive registrational study results in papillary NMIBC
detailed_catalyst_text: Peer-reviewed results from the Phase 2/3 QUILT-3.032 cohort B were published, reporting efficacy and safety of the combination in BCG-unresponsive high-grade papillary-only NMIBC. The study met its primary endpoint with a 12-month DFS rate of 58.2%, showed strong DSS and PFS at 36 months, high cystectomy avoidance, and a tolerable safety profile. These data address a high unmet need where no approved therapies exist for papillary-only disease after BCG failure.
catalyst_text_evidence: Results from the QUILT-3.032 study of 80 subjects, published in The Journal of Urology, showed 96% disease-specific survival and 83% progression-free survival at 36 months, demonstrating the long-term duration of effect of ANKTIVA® in patients with high-grade papillary NMIBC without CIS. Specific key efficacy findings from cohort B (N=80) of the Phase 2/3 open-label, single-arm multi-center QUILT-3.032 study include: The DFS rate at 12 months (primary endpoint) was 58.2% (95% CI 46.6, 68.2); corresponding rates at 24 and 36 months were 52.1% (95% CI 40.3, 62.7) and 38.2% (95% CI 25.6, 50.6). PFS rates were 94.9% (95% CI 86.9, 98.0) at 12 months and 83.1% (95% CI 69.5, 91.0) at 36 months. Cystectomy avoidance rates at 12 and 36 months were 92.2% (95% CI 83.4, 96.4) and 81.8% (95% CI 68.1, 90.1). The safety profile of ANKTIVA plus BCG, which was assessed for study cohorts A and B (N=180), was tolerable and consistent with BCG alone. Grade 1 or 2 TRAEs were seen in 61% of patients, with grade 3 events observed in 3% and no grade 4 or 5 events.
